defects.name: Stringing
defects.summary: Thin strands appear between travel moves or separate features.

questions.text: Where do the strings show up most?

options.label: Between open gaps or separate features

questions.text: Did this start after changing filament or nozzle temperature?
Is retraction enabled and known-good in this slicer profile?

causes.title: Retraction is too low or disabled
Nozzle temperature is too high
Travel path or travel speed needs tuning

actions: Restore the printer-appropriate retraction default, then retest.
Lower nozzle temperature by 5 to 10 C if the filament still strings.
Increase travel speed or reduce travel over open gaps if your slicer exposes those controls.
guardrails: First-layer settings unless the strings only appear on layer one
notes: PETG and wet filament string more easily than PLA.
Bowden printers usually need more retraction than direct-drive printers.

defects.name: Poor first layer adhesion
defects.summary: The print does not stick, peels up early, or leaves broken first-layer lines.

questions.text: What do the first-layer lines look like?

options.label: Good in some areas, bad in others

questions.text: Has the build plate been cleaned recently?
Is the bed temperature normal for this material?

causes.title: Nozzle is too far from the bed
Plate contamination or poor surface prep
Uneven bed mesh or local Z offset issue

actions: Wash the build plate with dish soap and warm water, then avoid touching the print area.
Adjust Z offset until lines are connected and lightly flattened.
Rerun bed mesh or automatic leveling if adhesion changes across the plate.
notes: Smooth plates need clean surfaces more than textured PEI.
ABS and ASA may also need enclosure temperature control.

defects.name: Warping
defects.summary: Corners or edges lift as the part cools.

questions.text: When does lifting start?
Is the printer exposed to drafts or a cool room?
Is the part broad, flat, or sharp-cornered?

causes.title: Cooling stress is pulling corners up
First layer is not anchoring the part
Material needs more thermal control

actions: Add a brim and retest with the same model orientation.
Reduce part cooling for the early layers if the material allows it.
Shield the printer from drafts or use an enclosure for high-shrink materials.
notes: PLA usually warps from surface prep or drafts.
ABS and ASA often require enclosure temperature control.

defects.name: Under-extrusion
defects.summary: Lines are thin, gaps appear, or the part looks starved for plastic.

questions.text: Is the missing plastic constant or intermittent?
Can the spool and filament path move freely?
Could the nozzle be partially clogged?

causes.title: Partial clog or restricted nozzle
Filament path drag
Retraction recovery is too aggressive

actions: Check spool movement and filament path before changing slicer settings.
Run a cold pull or nozzle cleaning routine if extrusion skips continue.
Raise nozzle temperature by 5 C only after ruling out drag or clogging.
notes: Grinding marks on filament point toward path drag or clogging.
Flexible filament is especially sensitive to feed path resistance.

defects.name: Over-extrusion
defects.summary: Surfaces look swollen, ridges build up, or dimensions come out oversized.

questions.text: Where is the excess material most visible?
Was flow, extrusion multiplier, or filament profile changed recently?
Are measured dimensions oversized?

causes.title: Flow multiplier is too high
First layer is too squished
Top solid layers are accumulating excess material

actions: Return flow or extrusion multiplier to the filament default, then retest.
If only layer one is swollen, raise Z offset slightly instead of changing global flow.
Run a single-wall flow calibration before making broad profile changes.
notes: Dimensional checks matter more than visual texture alone.
Do not fix elephant foot by lowering global flow unless the whole part is over-extruded.

defects.name: Ringing / ghosting
defects.summary: Echo-like ripples appear after corners, text, or sharp direction changes.

questions.text: Where are the echoes strongest?
Did this appear after increasing speed or acceleration?
Have belts, frame, or toolhead screws been checked recently?

causes.title: Acceleration or jerk is too aggressive
Belt tension or mechanical looseness
Input-shaping profile needs calibration

actions: Reduce acceleration for outer walls and retest the same model.
Check belt tension and toolhead/frame fasteners, especially on the affected axis.
Run input shaping or resonance calibration if your printer supports it.
notes: Ringing is mechanical or motion-related more often than material-related.
A single-axis pattern is a strong clue.

defects.name: Elephant foot
defects.summary: The bottom layers bulge outward and make the part base oversized.

questions.text: How many layers are affected?

options.label: Most of the part is oversized

questions.text: Does the first layer look heavily squished?
Is bed temperature higher than usual?

causes.title: First layer is too close to the bed
Bottom layers stay too soft
Global over-extrusion

actions: Raise Z offset slightly if the first layer is overly compressed.
Lower bed temperature a small amount after adhesion is reliable.
Use slicer elephant-foot compensation for dimension-critical parts.
notes: Do not trade away adhesion too aggressively.
If the whole part is oversized, diagnose flow instead.

defects.name: Layer shift
defects.summary: The print suddenly offsets on X or Y partway through.

questions.text: Is the shift mostly on one axis?
Did the nozzle hit curled plastic or a lifted edge?
Was speed or acceleration recently increased?

causes.title: Belt slip or loose pulley on the shifted axis
Nozzle collision knocked the print out of position
Motion settings exceed reliable limits

actions: Check belt tension and pulley grub screws on the shifted axis.
Look for curled corners or over-extruded ridges that the nozzle could hit.
Reduce acceleration and travel speed, then rerun the failed region if possible.
notes: Layer shifts are usually mechanical, motion, or collision problems.
A repeated shift height often points to a model feature or collision.

defects.name: Blobs / zits
defects.summary: Small bumps appear on outer walls, often near seams or travel starts.

questions.text: Where do blobs appear?
Could the filament be wet or popping?
Have seam, pressure advance, or coasting settings been changed?

causes.title: Seam start/stop pressure is not controlled
Wet filament or inconsistent extrusion
Cornering or acceleration changes are leaving extra material

actions: Make the seam visible and aligned so you can confirm whether blobs follow it.
Dry filament before tuning seam compensation if popping or random blobs appear.
Tune pressure advance or coasting only after temperature and filament state are stable.
notes: Random bumps are a different clue than seam-aligned bumps.
PETG often needs slower, calmer seam tuning than PLA.

defects.name: Bridging failure
defects.summary: Plastic sags or drops when crossing open spans.

questions.text: How long are the failed bridges?
Is part cooling enabled and strong for bridges?
Are bridge speed or bridge flow settings customized?

causes.title: Bridge cooling is too low
Bridge flow or speed needs tuning
Nozzle temperature is too hot for clean spans

actions: Increase bridge fan or part cooling for materials that tolerate it.
Lower bridge flow slightly if strands look thick and saggy.
Lower nozzle temperature by 5 C if even short bridges droop.
notes: Some materials bridge poorly even when tuned.
Model orientation can avoid impossible bridges.
